## NODE char_rama Character "Rama" "Ramayana" "Bala Kanda"
summary: Seventh avatar of Vishnu; prince of Ayodhya; hero of the Ramayana, exiled to the forest with his wife Sita.

## NODE char_sita Character "Sita" "Ramayana" "Aranya Kanda"
summary: Wife of Rama and avatar of Lakshmi; abducted by Ravana and rescued after a great war; embodiment of devotion and purity.

## NODE char_hanuman Character "Hanuman" "Ramayana" "Kishkindha Kanda"
summary: Vanara (monkey) devotee of Rama; son of Vayu; leapt to Lanka and found Sita; embodiment of bhakti (devotion).

## NODE char_ravana Character "Ravana" "Ramayana" "Aranya Kanda"
summary: Ten-headed demon king of Lanka; devotee of Shiva; abducted Sita, provoking the war with Rama.

## NODE char_krishna Character "Krishna" "Mahabharata" "Bhagavad Gita"
summary: Eighth avatar of Vishnu; charioteer and guide of Arjuna; speaker of the Bhagavad Gita; central figure of Hindu devotion.

## NODE char_arjuna Character "Arjuna" "Mahabharata" "Bhagavad Gita"
summary: Greatest archer of the Pandavas; cousin and friend of Krishna; faces moral crisis before the Kurukshetra War, resolved by Krishna's teaching.

## NODE char_shiva Character "Shiva" "Puranas" "Shiva Purana"
summary: The Destroyer in the Trimurti; lord of meditation, yoga, and transformation; his dance (tandava) sustains and destroys the cosmos.

## NODE char_vishnu Character "Vishnu" "Puranas" "Vishnu Purana"
summary: The Preserver in the Trimurti; descends as avatars (Rama, Krishna) to restore dharma; reclines on the cosmic serpent Shesha.

## NODE char_brahma Character "Brahma" "Puranas" "Brahma Purana"
summary: The Creator in the Trimurti; emerged from the lotus growing from Vishnu's navel; father of the Vedas.

## NODE char_indra Character "Indra" "Rig Veda" "Mandala 1"
summary: King of the gods and god of thunder and war in the Vedas; wielder of the vajra (thunderbolt); slayer of the serpent Vritra.

## NODE char_vasuki Character "Vasuki" "Mahabharata" "Adi Parva"
summary: King of the nagas (serpents); used as the churning rope in the churning of the ocean of milk (Samudra Manthan).

## NODE place_ayodhya Place "Ayodhya" "Ramayana" "Bala Kanda"
summary: Sacred city and birthplace of Rama; capital of the kingdom of Kosala; one of the seven holy cities of Hinduism.

## NODE place_lanka Place "Lanka" "Ramayana" "Yuddha Kanda"
summary: Island kingdom of Ravana; site of the great battle where Rama and his army defeated Ravana to rescue Sita.

## NODE place_bhogavati Place "Bhogavati" "Mahabharata" "Adi Parva"
summary: Subterranean capital of the nagas in Patala; ruled by Vasuki; described as a jeweled city in the Mahabharata.

## NODE place_kurukshetra Place "Kurukshetra" "Mahabharata" "Bhagavad Gita"
summary: The battlefield where the Kurukshetra War between the Pandavas and Kauravas was fought; Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita here.

## NODE event_kurukshetra_war Event "Kurukshetra War" "Mahabharata" "Bhishma Parva"
summary: The great war between the Pandavas and Kauravas; central event of the Mahabharata; Krishna's Bhagavad Gita precedes the battle.

## NODE event_abduction_sita Event "Abduction of Sita" "Ramayana" "Aranya Kanda"
summary: Ravana's kidnapping of Sita from the forest, disguised as a golden deer's ruse; triggered the Ramayana's war.

## NODE event_samudra_manthan Event "Churning of the Ocean of Milk" "Mahabharata" "Adi Parva"
summary: The gods and asuras churned the cosmic ocean using Vasuki and Mount Mandara to obtain amrita (the nectar of immortality).

## NODE obj_chakra Object "Sudarshana Chakra" "Mahabharata" "Vishnu Purana"
summary: The spinning discus weapon of Vishnu, wielded by Krishna; a symbol of cosmic order and divine power.

## NODE obj_bow_rama Object "Bow of Rama" "Ramayana" "Bala Kanda"
summary: The divine bow (Sharanga/Kodanda) wielded by Rama; used to defeat Ravana and complete his exile.

## NODE concept_dharma Concept "Dharma" "Mahabharata" "Bhagavad Gita"
summary: The cosmic law of righteousness, duty, and moral order; the central ethical concept Krishna teaches Arjuna.

## NODE concept_karma Concept "Karma" "Bhagavad Gita" "chapter 2"
summary: The law of cause and effect across lifetimes; action and its consequences binding the soul to samsara.

## NODE concept_trimurti Concept "Trimurti" "Puranas" "cosmology"
summary: The triad of Brahma (creator), Vishnu (preserver), and Shiva (destroyer) that governs the cycle of cosmic creation and dissolution.

## EDGE edge_shiva_worshipped char_shiva WORSHIPPED_AS char_ravana "Ramayana" "devotion"

## NODE char_durga Character "Durga" "Devi Mahatmya" "chapter 2"
summary: The warrior goddess; a form of Devi/Shakti; mounted on a lion or tiger; slew the buffalo demon Mahishasura when no male god could; embodiment of divine feminine power.

## NODE char_ganesha Character "Ganesha" "Ganesha Purana" "tradition"
summary: Elephant-headed god of beginnings, wisdom, and obstacle-removal; son of Shiva and Parvati; invoked at the start of any undertaking; scribe of the Mahabharata.

## NODE char_parvati Character "Parvati" "Shiva Purana" "tradition"
summary: Daughter of the mountain Himalaya; wife of Shiva; mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya; the benign aspect of the Great Goddess (Devi); embodiment of ascetic power and devotion.

## NODE char_kartikeya Character "Kartikeya (Murugan)" "Skanda Purana" "tradition"
summary: God of war; son of Shiva and Parvati; commander of the divine army; rides a peacock; slew the demon Tarakasura; widely worshipped in South India.

## NODE char_mahishasura Character "Mahishasura" "Devi Mahatmya" "chapter 2"
summary: Buffalo demon; received a boon that no man could slay; conquered the three worlds; slain by the goddess Durga in a great battle; embodiment of demonic arrogance.

## NODE char_tarakasura Character "Tarakasura" "Skanda Purana" "tradition"
summary: Demon who received a boon that only a son of Shiva could kill him; conquered the heavens; slain by Kartikeya, who was born specifically to defeat him.

## NODE char_bhishma Character "Bhishma" "Mahabharata" "Bhishma Parva"
summary: Grand patriarch of the Kuru dynasty; took a vow of lifelong celibacy (brahmacharya) so his father could marry; commander of the Kaurava army; fell on a bed of arrows.

## NODE char_draupadi Character "Draupadi" "Mahabharata" "Adi Parva"
summary: Wife of the five Pandava brothers; born from fire; princess of Panchala; her humiliation in the dice game triggered the Kurukshetra War; embodiment of feminine honor.

## NODE place_patala Place "Patala" "Mahabharata" "Adi Parva"
summary: The netherworld in Hindu cosmology; subterranean realm of the nagas; seven layers below the earth; where Bhogavati is located.

## NODE obj_gada Object "Gada of Bhima" "Mahabharata" "tradition"
summary: The mighty mace wielded by Bhima, the strongest of the Pandavas; used in the Kurukshetra War; symbol of raw physical strength.
